Recognize the approach

Collage combines separate visual fragments into a new composition.

Look for

  • Cut edges and visible layering
  • Mixed image scales
  • Overlaps with intentional focal points

Your learning goal

Describe the visual decisions before choosing a tool. Then make one small example that uses them deliberately.

Next: Origins

Where it comes from

Collage combines separate visual fragments into a new composition. On the web it can mix photography, scans, illustration, and lettering while keeping links and text independent.

What to examine

Look at the heading, one control, the image treatment, and the reading order. Explain which decisions establish the style and which make the page usable.

Next: Construction

How to construct it

  1. Mask original or licensed source images in an editor. Export fragments with transparency.
  2. Position fragments in a responsive composition; keep essential copy as HTML and preserve a simple reading order.

Small practice task

Combine three original photographs and one paper texture. Keep a consistent light direction or deliberately explain its absence.

Before you expand it

Test the result at its intended size, on a narrow screen, and with keyboard focus. Preserve editable layers and record the source and license of acquired assets.
